neighbours.label: A non-final piece inside a rare or long word that the tokenizer splits into several pieces (rare English words, long compounds, long foreign or misspelled words), in any language; the same sentence with a common short word in that spot, and plain text made of common whole words, stays low.
neighbours.short: inside a rare word split into pieces

neighbours.notes: Test sentences written blind by a second author from the label only (stream blind_test). The + pole is broad (40.7% of tokens reach 0.1 of max); plain sentences probed at 0.13-0.24, split-word twins at 0.31-0.67. Feeders L33/N10909+ (mid-piece of misspelled/split words) and L28/N11592- (a 'c' piece glued after punctuation) are word-fragment cells.

predictions: Most fire sentences 0.3-0.7; near misses mostly 0.1-0.25, with the sentence-initial ones the risk.
